Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Alok Ranjan Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mahesh Kumar Dubey,Tanisha Jahangir Monir,Yadvendra Y Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard Sri Alok Ranjan Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Dheeraj Kumar Dwivedi,
Ms. Sunita Chauhan holding brief of Ms. Tanisha Jahangir Monir on behalf of the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.112 of 2022, under sections 376(1) I.P.C. & Section 3 and 4 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act-2012, Police Station Derapur, District Kanpur Dehat, during the pendency of investigation/trial.

sentences.text: It is submitted that in this case applicant is employed in Indian Navy.

As per allegation in F.I.R. the victim used to come for coaching classes conducted by the present applicant three years prior to the Pradeep Pal vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58084748/
1 alleged incident and applicant developed affair with the victim and made promise to marry with her and also established physical relations.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This relationship continued for the aforesaid period and when he got employed in Indian Navy he refused to marry as a result present F.I.R. was lodged against him.
It is also submitted that the victim was major at the time of alleged incident and her age was found to be more than 18 years.
Further submitted that victim herself denied from being medically examined and there is nothing on record to support the allegation of physical relations with the victim by the present applicant.

It is also submitted that there was conversation regarding marriage of the victim with the applicant but it could not be settled that was the reason this F.I.R.
was lodged with false allegations of establishing physical relations with the victim three years ago.
Since after investigation charge sheet has been submitted and in pursuance thereof the applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case victim was minor at the time she was going to attend coaching classes conducted by the present applicant.
Further urged that on the pretext of marriage the applicant developed physical relations with victim which cannot be said to be consensus and later on he refused to marry.
It is also urged that during investigation the age of the victim was found to be minor as a result POCSO Act was also added.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the nature of allegations and gravity of offences,
there appears no ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of this applicant.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is, hereby, rejected.
